newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico June CPI rises 0.89 percent-Banco de Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Mexico June CPI rises 0.89 percent-Banco de Mexico.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 0.89 percent in June from the month before after rising 0.91 percent in May, Banco de Mexico said.
The central bank added that the producer price index rose 0.78 percent in June from the month before, compared to a rise of 0.69 percent in May.
A poll conducted by Reuters of 13 Mexico City brokerages and research firms had found expectations of a rise of 0.90 percent in consumer inflation in June.
The central bank said the rise in consumer prices was about half of what it was in June last year when the CPI rose 1.63 percent.
It said consumer price inflation in the first six months of the year was 8.66 percent, compared to 15.31 percent in the first half of 1996.
The year-over-year increase in consumer prices was 20.35 percent, the central bank said.
It said that the main cause of inflation this year was an increase in prices of housing rental costs, domestic gas, local telephone services, soft drinks and other products.
It said the basic basket of consumer goods rose 0.85 percent in June.
Banco de Mexico gave the following breakdown for June:
INDEX Percent
Food, drinks and tobacco 0.47
Clothing and shoes 1.20
Housing 1.30
Furniture 1.22
Health and personal care 1.33
Transportation 0.71
Education 0.75
Other services 1.10
The accumulated increase for the first six months for the producer price index was 7.06 percent, compared with 14.10 percent in the same period a year earlier.
Ona year-over-year basis consumer prices rose 17.06 percent.
